The largest such m is 32. I did not derive this here; it is the answer I recall for this known competition problem. I only checked the simple bound m ≤ 35, which is weaker than 32.

The bound comes from the following. The two rows with m red cells each contain 2m red cells, and these cells must lie in columns with pairwise distinct red counts. So there are at least 2m columns with distinct counts, which forces 2m ≤ 70 and so m ≤ 35. Tightening this to 32 needs a finer counting argument and a construction that I did not carry out.

ANSWER: 32
